_comment: HBM3 16Gb die, 8-high stack (16 GB/stack). Organization from ramulator2 v2.1 python/ramulator/dram/hbm3.py (HBM3_16Gb_8hi). Basis for H200-class HBM3E modeling at 6.4 Gbps. The engine simulates one pseudo-channel; channels_per_stack/stacks/SID scale device totals only, not per-PC energy. HBM3 stack-ID (SID=2 for 8hi) is not modeled here.
_comment_columns: ramulator (1<<5)<<3 = 256; 'HBM CA already takes BL into account'. Metadata only (not used in core energy).
_comment_width: per-pseudochannel DQ width in bits (ramulator dq=32). Metadata only (not used in core energy).
_comment_dataRate: transfers per tCK. HBM3 drives the data bus from WCK at 2*f(CK), DDR on WCK => 4 transfers per CK cycle (6.4 GT/s at tCK=625ps). So tBurst = nBL/dataRate = 8/4 = 2 cycles = 1.25 ns for a 256-bit (BL8 x 32 DQ) read; full BW ~= 4.9 TB/s across 192 PC.
